newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fire destroys 11,000 tonnes of Dutch cocoa.
newsitem.headline: Fire destroys 11,000 tonnes of Dutch cocoa.

text.p: A fire on Saturday night at a cocoa warehouse just outside Amsterdam destroyed around 11,000 tonnes of cocoa, a spokesman for the warehouse's owner Unicontrol told Reuters on Monday.
"There was a huge fire on Saturday night. The warehouse is totally destroyed," Unicontrol spokesman Eugene Bleekemolen said.
He said most of the cocoa was Ivorian in origin and destined for the London terminal market.
The main owners were Phibro as well as Dutch grinders Gerkens Cacao and Cacao de Zaan.
The reason for the blaze was still being investigated, he added.
The fire was still burning at the warehouse as the jute sacks used to store the cocoa made it very difficult for fire-fighters to put out the blaze.
The fire service had estimated it would remain at the scene for another 10 days, Bleekemolen said.
He had no other details and no one was immediately available for comment at Gerkens.
A spokesman for Cacao de Zaan confirmed that the firm owned some of the cocoa, but said it had only a small share.
The warehouse was situated in Wormerveer, near Zaandam.
